title: Ignition Failure / No Flame
shortDescription: Greenstar boiler failed to detect flame after ignition retries.
fullDescription:
EA (sometimes shown as 227) is the Worcester Bosch Greenstar ignition lockout. The boiler attempts ignition three times and then locks out if flame is not detected.

Common causes: closed gas valve, fouled flame rod, low gas supply pressure, plugged condensate trap with frozen condensate in cold weather.
safetyWarning: If you smell gas, evacuate and call 0800 111 999.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm another gas appliance works.

fixSteps.title: Thaw condensate pipe
fixSteps.instruction: If condensate pipe runs outside, thaw with warm cloth (NOT boiling water).

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset.

whenToCallPro: Gas Safe engineer for gas pressure work.

faq.a: Yes — first cold snap in October/November is the peak season for EA.

title: Overheat / High Limit
shortDescription: Heat exchanger exceeded the safety thermostat trip point.
fullDescription:
E9 indicates the Greenstar safety thermostat opened. Causes are loss of flow (failed pump, closed isolation, air-bound HX) or heat exchanger fouled with limescale.

In hard-water areas E9 is often the precursor to a HX replacement; an annual service with limescale inhibitor is recommended.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the safety thermostat.

fixSteps.title: Verify isolation
fixSteps.instruction: Check both flow and return service valves are open.

fixSteps.title: Bleed radiators
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed all radiators and the system.

whenToCallPro: HX descale or pump replacement.

faq.a: Fit a magnetic filter and use a chemical inhibitor.

title: Fan Fault
shortDescription: Combustion fan stopped running during a heat call.
fullDescription: C1 indicates the fan stopped or did not reach the required speed. Common on older Greenstars where the fan motor brushes wear out.
safetyWarning: Mains isolation required before fan work.
symptoms: No fan sound or weak fan

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat fan PWM and tach connectors.

fixSteps.title: Schedule replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Gas Safe engineer to swap fan.

whenToCallPro: Fan replacement.

faq.a: 8-12 years on Greenstar.

title: Internal Control Fault
shortDescription: PCB self-test failed.
fullDescription: E1 is a generic Worcester Bosch PCB fault. A single occurrence may clear with a power cycle; repeat E1 needs PCB replacement.
safetyWarning: Mains isolation before opening cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off at the spur for 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Gas Safe engineer for PCB swap.

whenToCallPro: Always for PCB.

faq.a: Yes — recommended.

title: Internal Communication Error
shortDescription: PCB communication fault.
fullDescription: F0 indicates a communication fault between PCB and display, or between safety chips. Power cycle clears most cases.
safetyWarning: Mains isolation before any work.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off at the spur 2 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Always for PCB.

faq.a: Often.

title: Flame Signal Persists
shortDescription: Flame seen with gas off.
fullDescription: F7 indicates the control sees a flame signal when the gas valve is closed. Treat as a possible stuck gas valve or moisture on ignition assembly.
safetyWarning: Treat as gas-valve safety event.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off at spur 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Gas Safe engineer.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: Damp basement installs are at higher risk.

title: Low Pressure
shortDescription: System pressure below minimum.
fullDescription:
H07 is the Greenstar low-pressure warning. Top up via the filling key or external loop to 1.0-1.5 bar cold.

Unlike F.22 on Vaillant, H07 is a warning rather than full lockout on some Greenstar models — boiler may still run briefly.
safetyWarning: Do not exceed 2 bar.

fixSteps.title: Top up
fixSteps.instruction: Use filling key to bring pressure to 1.2 bar.

fixSteps.title: Look for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect radiators and PRV outlet.

whenToCallPro: Hidden leak.

faq.a: Means a leak.

title: No Flame Detected (Numeric)
shortDescription: Newer Greenstar models show 227 instead of EA for ignition lockout.
fullDescription:
227 is the numeric equivalent of EA on later Greenstar firmware. Same root causes — closed gas, frozen condensate, fouled ignition rod, low gas pressure.

Reset via the long-press of the reset button. Three failed attempts within an hour locks out the boiler for ~24 minutes before allowing reset.
safetyWarning: If gas odor present, evacuate and call 0800 111 999.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm meter open.

fixSteps.title: Thaw condensate pipe
fixSteps.instruction: Thaw with warm cloth.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset button until display clears.

whenToCallPro: Gas pressure verification.

faq.a: Newer firmware uses numeric codes; functionally identical.

title: Fan Fault
shortDescription: The combustion fan is not running at the speed commanded by the PCB.
fullDescription:
Fault C7 on Worcester Greenstar boilers indicates the combustion fan is failing to reach the target RPM. The boiler will lock out before ignition for safety.

Causes include a worn fan motor, a loose fan harness, or a failed PCB driver. The fan is often replaceable as a unit.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Loud fan noise prior to fault

fixSteps.title: Reset and Listen
fixSteps.instruction: Reset the boiler. If you hear no fan or a grinding fan, leave it off and call an engineer.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer reseats the fan harness and verifies wiring continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer replaces the fan assembly and verifies CO2 with a flue gas analyzer.

whenToCallPro: Always have a Gas Safe engineer perform fan replacement; combustion must be re-verified afterwards.

faq.q: Is fan replacement covered by warranty?
faq.a: Usually yes within the Worcester Greenstar parts warranty (5-10 years depending on registration).

title: Diverter Valve Fault
shortDescription: The three-way diverter valve has not changed position as commanded.
fullDescription: Fault D5 on Worcester combi boilers indicates the diverter actuator failed to switch between heating and DHW positions. Common causes are a stuck mechanical valve (often from sludge), a failed actuator, or wiring issues.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Hot water but no heat (or vice versa)

fixSteps.title: Engineer Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer manually exercises the diverter and inspects for sludge.

fixSteps.title: Power Flush / Replace Valve
fixSteps.instruction: If sludge is present, a power flush plus inhibitor; if mechanical, replace diverter assembly.

whenToCallPro: Diverter valve work involves draining the boiler and resealing; have a Gas Safe engineer perform this.

faq.a: It can prevent recurrence but rarely frees an already seized diverter; mechanical service is usually needed.

title: DHW Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Domestic hot water (DHW) NTC sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Fault E2 on Worcester Greenstar boilers indicates a fault on the DHW outlet temperature sensor. The boiler may continue to provide heating but DHW will be unreliable.

Causes are a disconnected/failed sensor or wiring damage.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat DHW sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Test/Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer tests resistance and replaces if failed.

whenToCallPro: If reseating the connector does not clear the fault, an engineer should replace the NTC.

faq.q: Can I shower with E2 active?
faq.a: Outlet temperatures may swing; not recommended until fixed.

title: Heating Flow Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Central heating flow NTC fault (open or shorted).
fullDescription:
Fault E3 indicates the central heating flow temperature sensor is reading out of range. The boiler will lock out heating to protect the heat exchanger.

The NTC and harness should be tested first; the boiler often clears once the sensor or wiring is restored.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat heating flow NTC plug.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer replaces NTC if test confirms failure.

whenToCallPro: Replacement of the NTC should be done by a Gas Safe engineer with the boiler isolated.

faq.q: Why does E3 happen in cold weather?
faq.a: Cold weather can stress weak connections; reseating often helps.

title: Boiler Overheat / Limit Trip
shortDescription: The overheat thermostat or sensor logic has tripped.
fullDescription:
Fault E5 on Worcester Greenstar boilers indicates an overheat condition has been detected, similar to F.20 on Vaillant. The cause is almost always a flow problem.

Check system pressure (1-1.5 bar cold), bleed radiators, and verify the pump operates. Persistent E5 may indicate a scaled heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Check Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Verify gauge reads 1.0-1.5 bar cold; top up via filling loop if low.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Radiators
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed each radiator starting from the lowest floor.

fixSteps.title: Engineer Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: If recurring, engineer tests pump and inspects heat exchanger for scale.

whenToCallPro: Persistent overheats can permanently damage the heat exchanger; have an engineer diagnose flow issues quickly.

faq.q: How often should I bleed radiators?
faq.a: Annually, or whenever you notice cold spots at the top of a radiator.

title: Heating Return Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Central heating return NTC reading out of range.
fullDescription:
Fault E6 indicates a problem with the central heating return temperature sensor. The boiler cannot accurately calculate flow/return delta T and will lock out heating.

Causes mirror E3 but on the return side.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat return NTC plug.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer replaces NTC if testing confirms failure.

whenToCallPro: If reseating fails, have an engineer test and replace the NTC.

faq.q: Can I just disconnect the sensor?
faq.a: No. The boiler will not run without valid sensor readings.

title: Flue Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Flue gas temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Fault E7 indicates the flue gas thermistor is reading out of range. Worcester Greenstar boilers monitor flue temperature to detect heat exchanger blockages and prevent overheating the flue.

Most causes are sensor or wiring related; rarely the flue itself is overheated due to scaled HX.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Boiler shuts down on long heat calls

fixSteps.title: Engineer Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer inspects flue NTC and wiring at the flue elbow.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if out of spec.

whenToCallPro: Flue gas sensors are inside the appliance casing; replacement should be done by a Gas Safe engineer.

faq.a: Yes. The boiler limits flue temperature to protect plastic flue components and to prevent fire risk.

title: Outdoor Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor temperature sensor (weather compensation) is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Information code H37 on Worcester Greenstar boilers with weather compensation indicates a fault on the external temperature sensor. The boiler will revert to a default flow temperature curve until repaired.

Fault is usually wiring or sensor related, especially after winter weather.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Heating runs at fixed flow temperature

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect the outdoor sensor on the wall for damage.

fixSteps.title: Test and Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer tests resistance and replaces if open/shorted.

whenToCallPro: Have an engineer install a new sensor and weatherproof the splice if you cannot DIY safely.

faq.q: Will heating still work without weather comp?
faq.a: Yes, but at a fixed flow temperature, which is less efficient.

title: Boiler Communication Fault
shortDescription: Loss of communication between the boiler and the programmer/controller.
fullDescription:
Information code H62 on Worcester Greenstar boilers indicates loss of communication between the appliance and the wired/wireless controller (Wave, Comfort+, EasyControl).

Causes include controller battery exhaustion, weak wireless signal, damaged controller wiring, or a paired device that has been moved out of range.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.

fixSteps.title: Replace Controller Batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Replace controller batteries with fresh alkaline cells.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair Controller
fixSteps.instruction: Follow the controller pairing procedure from the boiler menu.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If wired, check for damaged or pinched cable from controller to boiler.

whenToCallPro: If a new battery and re-pairing do not resolve H62, have a Worcester-trained engineer test the controller and boiler comm board.

faq.a: Yes, the boiler has a built-in mode for manual heating; check the appliance manual for the exact button sequence.

title: Diverter Valve Stuck
shortDescription: The internal three-way diverter valve has not switched between heating and DHW.
fullDescription:
Fault A21 on Worcester Greenstar boilers indicates the diverter valve actuator is not changing position when commanded. The most common cause is a mechanically seized diverter spindle, often due to system sludge or scale.

DIY remedies are limited; the boiler usually needs an engineer to manually exercise or replace the diverter and treat the system with inhibitor.
safetyWarning: This error involves a gas-fired appliance. If you smell gas at any time, do not operate switches or attempt repairs. Evacuate, leave doors open, and call your gas utility from a safe location. Repairs to gas valves, burners, or flue components must be performed by a licensed gas engineer or technician.
symptoms: Hot water but no heat (or vice versa)

fixSteps.title: Engineer Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Engineer manually moves the diverter and inspects for sludge.

fixSteps.title: Power Flush
fixSteps.instruction: If sludge is present, perform a power flush and add a Worcester-approved inhibitor.

fixSteps.title: Replace Diverter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the diverter assembly if mechanically failed.

whenToCallPro: Always have a Gas Safe engineer perform diverter replacement and add a system inhibitor afterwards.

faq.a: Annual servicing, magnetic system filter, and adequate inhibitor concentration significantly reduce the risk.
